summary: Initial POC scoping to pick open-model shortlist for a 2-week benchmark pilot focused on domain-adapted clinical QA and multilingual support. Discussed success metrics (exact-match/F1 for QA, latency < 450ms p50, cost per 1k tokens), dataset slices, infra constraints (VPC, data residency), and timelines for sandbox + bench. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 09:57 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Aria Gomez (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Head of ML, Cascade), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Sofia Rivera (Data Engineer), Marcus Lee (Privacy Lead)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we put together a short agenda, we'll do a quick intro, go over your goals and success criteria for the POC, then model shortlist and bench plan, and finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:06] Priya: Yeah sounds good. Thanks Maya. Sorry we had a last minute swap so Liam is on.
[00:11] Liam: Hi all, thanks, quick note on timing we have leadership review on 11/20 so ideally we want results from the pilot by 11/17ish. Is that feasible?
[00:18] Daniel: We should be able to get a 2-week sandbox and run the main bench in that window. We'll size the workloads and focus on the highest priority slices you specify.
[00:25] Sofia: To be clear our core use case is clinical Q&A: triage question answering over our knowledge base + patient notes. Also multilingual - EN, ES, PT - with a 10% Spanish/Portuguese traffic mix.
[00:39] Marcus: And on security side we need to validate VPC private deployment options and ensure logs don't leave region. We also want to confirm Redwood's KMS integration.
[00:48] Aria: Quick clarifying q: when you say logs don't leave region, do you mean audit logs or model prompts as well?
[00:55] Marcus: Both ideally, prompts are particularly sensitive. We might provide redacted samples for benchmarking.
[01:02] Maya: Great, we'll note that. Moving to success metrics — what would success look like at the end of the POC? Priya, can you start?
[01:11] Priya: Two things: quality and stability. For quality we want at least 84% exact-match on our closed-domain QA dev set or F1 > 0.88 depending on metric. Latency targets: p50 < 450ms, p95 < 1.2s for the production slice. Cost is also a tie-breaker; we prefer solutions that are >=20% cheaper than our current baseline.
[01:30] Daniel: Noted. We'll record p50/p95 across all model candidates and include per-token cost estimates for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options.
[01:40] Liam: Quick Q on cost — what are the levers we can expect to tune during the POC? Quantization? Batching? Caching?
[01:46] Aria: Yes all of those. Redwood Optimize will suggest batch sizing and KV prefix caching. We can also evaluate INT8 quantized variants during bench. We'll capture throughput/latency tradeoffs for each config.
[01:56] Priya: On dataset — we'll provide 2k redacted clinical Qs + anonymized notes. We'll identify the Spanish/Portuguese subset. Sofia will share via secure bucket.
[02:05] Sofia: I'll share a small sample today and the full 2k by Friday.
[02:09] Maya: Great. Let's talk model shortlist. Based on your needs (open models, clinical domain, multilingual), our initial candidates are: Llama-3-16b (quantized variants), Mistral-7B-Instruct, XGen-16B, and a domain-adapted 13B open LLM we can spin up (we call it 'redwood-13b-clinical' internally for the POC). We can also include a multilingual specialist model like BloomZ-7B for ES/PT.
[02:32] Priya: Hmm could you explain the quality tradeoffs? We worry about hallucinations on clinical facts.
[02:37] Daniel: Sure — big picture: larger context models like Llama-3-16b typically give stronger closed-domain QA out of the box but cost more. Mistral-7B is cheaper and surprisingly good with instruction tuning but struggles a bit with long-form context and may hallucinate more on niche clinical terms without domain fine-tuning. BloomZ gives better multilingual out-of-the-box for ES/PT but lower English QA performance in some of our internal tests. The redwood-13b-clinical is a model variant we pre-finetuned on public med datasets; it often hits a good precision/recall balance for clinical QA at moderate cost.
[03:09] Priya: That's helpful. For hallucination control can we instrument grounding or retrieval-augmented generation in the POC?
[03:15] Aria: Absolutely — we can plug a simple RAG setup against your knowledge base; we'll test both direct generation and RAG+verify modes. That will be one of our bench axes.
[03:22] Marcus: On compliance — does the Redwood sandbox support private networking? We don't want data egress.
[03:27] Ravi: For the sandbox we offer a VPC-attached private deployment for POC customers; logs can be restricted to your region and we support KMS. For a full Private deployment we'd provide the customer-managed control plane. We'll send the architecture note.
[03:39] Liam: Good. On workload sizing: our production expected QPS is small initially — 10 concurrent users, ~0.8 queries/sec peak, average 2k tokens per request due to long notes. But we want to bench at 5x to 10x load to understand headroom.
[03:54] Daniel: So we'll run benches at your nominal load (1x), at 5x and at 10x. We'll simulate the mixed language distribution and include heavy context lengths to stress KV cache. We'll report on tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and memory pressure (GPU RAM) per model variant.
[04:11] Priya: For the POC timeline we have roughly 14 days. Day 0-2: sandbox + model provisioning; day 3-9: run benches and iterate; day 10-12: evaluation and a short stabilization test; day 13-14: final results and exec summary.
[04:24] Maya: That aligns with leadership timing. We'll draft a detailed bench plan and a sheet with the exact test vectors and scoring.
[04:30] Sofia: Can you include the scoring rubric? We use a weighted score: 0.5 quality (F1/EM), 0.2 latency, 0.2 cost, 0.1 reliability.
[04:38] Maya: Yes we'll include that.
[04:40] Priya: A few more questions on tooling: can Redwood run token-level breakdowns? We want to see where time is spent (decode vs kernel time) and breakdown by batching.
[04:48] Aria: We can provide per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns from the Console; SEs can also attach flamegraph-like kernel timing from the runtime to help optimize batch size.
[04:57] Marcus: Also need proof of SOC2 and details on data retention policies.
[05:02] Ravi: We'll attach SOC 2 cert and a short FAQ for retention/retention deletion endpoints.
[05:07] Liam: Are there any hard blockers you foresee on the Redwood side for this POC?
[05:12] Daniel: Not really; the main risk is model availability in the exact quantized variant during the bench window. We'll pre-provision model artifacts as much as possible. If a variant isn't available, we'll fallback to the nearest compatible one and note it in the report.
[05:25] Priya: Regarding multilingual testing — we also want to test a few Portuguese clinical terms that are domain-specific. Will you need additional samples?
[05:31] Maya: If you can surface 30-50 Portuguese examples that would help.
[05:36] Sofia: We have those, will include in the dataset.
[05:39] Priya: About scoring: besides EM/F1, can you calculate calibration metrics or answer confidence? Sometimes the model is right but overconfident.
[05:47] Aria: Yes we can capture model logit-derived confidence and correlate with correctness. We'll include a small false-positive/false-negative breakdown.
[05:55] Liam: For the deployment mode, is Dedicated necessary for this pilot or Hosted is sufficient?
[06:00] Daniel: For benchmarking Hosted is fine; if you want to mirror production privacy constraints we'll use a VPC-attached private sandbox (which is similar to Redwood Private but quicker to provision for POC). Dedicated is more for predictable committed throughput at scale.
[06:12] Marcus: We might need Dedicated later but for the POC we'll try the private sandbox.
[06:16] Maya: OK, let's capture explicit next steps. I'll read them out and you interrupt if anything missing. Redwood will: 1) Send model shortlist + bench spreadsheet by Friday 11/06; 2) Provision VPC sandbox and pre-load the four candidates; 3) Share SOC2, KMS & deployment notes; 4) Schedule technical deep-dive for 11/10. Cascade will: share redacted dataset 2k by 11/06, provide Portuguese test slice, and confirm security contact.
[06:44] Priya: That matches. One last note on competitors — we benchmarked a hosted Anthropic model last quarter; we'd like Redwood to include a lightweight baseline (OpenAI or Anthropic) if license permits, just to see parity.
[06:58] Aria: We can include a baseline from our catalog if we have access; we'll note which baselines are vendor-hosted vs open-model.
[07:04] Liam: Thanks. Anything else?
[07:07] Sofia: No, thanks everyone.
[07:09] Maya: Great we'll follow up in email. Thanks all for your time.
[07:13] End meeting

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap, some terms transcribed incorrectly (e.g., KV cash instead of KV cache, redwood dedicate instead of Dedicated). There are deliberate minor transcription artifacts to preserve realism.
